work_completed:
- **S6, a candidate that cannot be isolated.** `batch._entangled` refuses with `CANDIDATE_NOT_ISOLATED` when two candidates share commits past the base (one built on the other, or both on a shared unmerged commit). In that case the build without one candidate still holds its work, so it could never be isolated; before this fix the batch fell through to `BATCH_UNEXPLAINED`. The check runs before anything else, even when the run would be green. It names the candidate whose work the other holds, and the refusal details include `shares_with`. Every refusal of the scoped batch (`isolate`, or `run` in a scoped project) now also prints `<CODE>: <reason>` on stderr; the strict batch prints exactly as before.
- **S4, three rounds for a load-sensitive red.** `attribution.load_sensitive` now matches a `latency` entry in every form the serial phase accepts:
  - an entry that names the file, the node id, a parametrised id, or a folder (with or without a trailing `/`);
  - a leading `./`, a tab before ` #`, or a byte-order mark;
  - the kind read as the word after the route whatever follows it (`latency`, `latency (x): r`, `Latency`), or as the first word when the route is left out.

  A load-sensitive red also gets its 3 rounds on the head without the change even when a full green nightly of that head would have stood in for that side. Before this, only one value was copied from the nightly record.
- **S2, a governance file alone.** On the wider change, the green record's own file is always in the change, because it is committed after the head it names. I added `select._bookkeeping`: when a change holds governance files, no code, and only bookkeeping records, those records select nothing. A change like that now selects nothing; any other record beside it still selects `record_reading` alone.
- The evidence notes are in `docs/research/W2-115-smart-close.md` under "eng-3".

- S6, choice I made: candidates that overlap are refused before anything runs, even when the batch would be green. This is the KPI's literal reading ("a candidate that cannot be isolated refuses the batch") and it fails closed.
- S2, choice I made: the narrowest fail-closed reading of "bookkeeping".
  - It covers only this ticket's `.tickets/<id>.md`, its own `docs/close/<id>/` and `docs/checkpoints/<id>/`, and the green records the change is counted from.
  - It applies only when the change holds a governance file and no code.
  - Another ticket's file or record still selects `record_reading`, so does bookkeeping on its own (the "records alone" rule), and a change with code is unchanged.
- The repo's `tests/conftest.py` "rep:" lists keep only the first row of a parametrised test in a whole-file run, which is why the new parametrised tests were also run by node id.
